correctness.rationale: Görtz–Yu Proposition 2.5 recalls the elementary-sequence containment equivalence φ_h=0 with h=g−floor(g/2). Muller's (1) and (5) match the permutation and dimension; Definitions 1.3–1.5 and Theorem 1.7 confirm the arrow direction, good-to-bad reachability requirement and odd-characteristic nonemptiness test. The first h indices have weights at least k+1; the only exceptions to containment at weights k+1 and k+2 are e_h, then e_(h−1) and e_h+e_g. For e_j, j≤h, the alternating orbit runs 1,g,2,g−1,…,j (singleton when j=1); π(j)=1 and the unique one leaves 2j−2 zeros. This is bad and no other cycle has a source one. Turning on g in e_h changes no permutation value, since both rules send g to 2. Now h→1→g is one intervening zero and the returning arc has 2h−4 zeros, so the cycle is good and all other cycles have no ones. This gives contact but not containment (φ_h=1). For g=3 the singletons and (1,3,2) give the same disjoint and mixed decisions without degeneracy. The finite checker is corroborative, not used as the general proof.
residual_risks: The argument uses the published geometric criteria, not an independent proof of them. No claim for characteristic two or other moduli problems.

evidence: The published genus counts are totals and give no dimension minima. The genus-five EO/Newton data distinguish the disjoint sequences (0,0,1,1,1), (0,1,1,1,1) and the supersingular contact for (0,0,1,1,2).
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: The fixed-genus case is covered, but counts and finite tables do not imply the result for arbitrary g.

originality.rationale: Existing containment, intersection criteria and small-genus results are credited. The distinct claim is the uniform extremal classification, with the two first-contact dimensions and exact exception types obtained by an exhaustive weight argument and symbolic analysis of the changing cycle.
residual_risks: Bounded searches and relevant full-text passages do not exclude an unindexed extremal corollary. Fixed genera and the general geometric criteria are not novelty claims.
